title: APIForge vs Swagger Editor: Feature & Usability Breakdown
description: Swagger Editor writes and validates specs. APIForge scores, tests and generates from them. See what each does, where each wins, and when to use both.
heroSubtitle: A spec authoring tool and a spec testing and scoring workbench
verdict:
Use Swagger Editor to write and edit a spec, to generate server stubs and client libraries in many languages, or to run everything on your own machine. Use APIForge after a spec exists: load a published spec from a URL, score its design, send requests with a CORS fallback, check responses against the schema and generate tests.

The two tools overlap less than their names suggest, and many teams will use both. We checked the Swagger Editor claims below against Swagger's own pages; where those pages say nothing, the table says so.

sections.title: Writing and editing a spec
sections.description:
Swagger Editor is built for authoring. It offers auto-completion while you type, validates your syntax for OpenAPI compliance as you write, and renders the result next to the text. If you are creating or changing a spec by hand, that loop is what you want.

APIForge has no editor. It starts from a spec that already exists and helps you understand and judge it. A typical sequence is to write in Swagger Editor, publish the file, then load the published URL in APIForge to see how the API scores and behaves. The [guide to validating Swagger and OpenAPI specs](/guides/validate-swagger-openapi-spec) covers the checks to run between those two steps.
sections.apiforgeWay: Loads a finished spec and does not change it
sections.competitorWay: Edits the spec with live validation and preview

sections.title: Spec versions and formats
sections.description:
Swagger's README lists OpenAPI 2.0, 3.0, 3.1 and 3.2, plus AsyncAPI 2.x and 3.x, in JSON and YAML. That is the wider range, and AsyncAPI support has no counterpart in APIForge.

APIForge reads Swagger 2.0 and OpenAPI 3.x. We ran nine version variants through its parser, including 3.2.0, a missing version field, and the unquoted numbers swagger: 2 and openapi: 3 that make Swagger UI fail, and every variant loaded with its endpoint. That leniency helps when a spec will not render elsewhere. It also means APIForge will not warn you about the bad version line; [Swagger UI unable to render this definition](/guides/swagger-ui-unable-to-render-definition) explains how to catch it. The [Swagger vs OpenAPI guide](/guides/swagger-vs-openapi) covers how the two format families differ.

sections.title: Testing requests and CORS
sections.description:
Both tools can send a request to your API. Swagger's documentation says Try it out needs CORS enabled on the API endpoints, and that custom headers such as Authorization must be listed in the server's allowed headers. Without that, the request fails with Failed to fetch. We tested nine server setups to see exactly which headers fix it, and the results are in [Swagger UI Failed to Fetch: causes and fixes](/guides/swagger-ui-failed-to-fetch).

APIForge's [testing workbench](/api-testing) tries the browser first. When the browser reports a CORS or network failure, it falls back to a server-side proxy. In our test the proxy returned 200 for three setups that blocked the browser. Three trade-offs apply: your request, including any token, passes through APIForge's server, the proxy cannot reach an API that exists only on your machine, and requests are capped at 30 seconds, 5 MB and 60 per minute.
sections.apiforgeWay: Browser first, then a server proxy when CORS blocks it
sections.competitorWay: Try it out from the browser, which needs CORS on the API

sections.title: Quality, validation and fixing
sections.description:
Swagger Editor validates that your spec follows the OpenAPI rules. A spec can pass that check and still be hard to use: verbs in paths, no documented error responses, no versioning.

APIForge scores design on seven pillars: naming, HTTP semantics, structure, consistency, versioning, error handling and documentation. The score comes from fixed rules. A small example spec with a path called /api/createOrder, two operations without error responses and no version prefix scored 78 out of 100, and the [API quality score](/api-score) listed each issue with a suggested fix. APIForge also offers an auto-fix preview that proposes path and method changes in the REST style, and it checks live responses against the response schema.
sections.apiforgeWay: Rule-based 0-100 score, auto-fix preview and response checks

sections.title: Code and test generation
sections.description:
Swagger Editor generates server stubs and client libraries in every popular language, according to Swagger. These are deterministic generators: the same spec produces the same code.

APIForge generates TypeScript types, IDE prompts, example payloads and a test matrix with AI. The output is fast to get and still needs a human read. APIForge says its AI features currently run on community free-tier models with strict rate limits, so expect limits on large specs. Test cases export to cURL, JavaScript fetch, JSON and a Postman collection. The [guide to generating test cases from an OpenAPI spec](/guides/generate-test-cases-from-openapi) shows how to judge them.
sections.apiforgeWay: AI-written types, payloads and tests, to be reviewed
sections.competitorWay: Deterministic server stubs and client libraries

sections.title: Privacy, hosting and teams
sections.description:
Swagger Editor runs as a hosted app at editor.swagger.io and can also run locally through Docker or npm, so a private spec never has to leave your machine. Swagger lists collaboration and hosted documentation under its Swagger for Teams offering.

APIForge is a hosted web app with no accounts and no team features yet. When you paste a spec URL or upload a file, APIForge's server fetches and parses it. Do not load an internal spec you are not willing to send to a third-party server. For private specs, run Swagger Editor locally.
sections.apiforgeWay: Hosted only, no accounts, server parses your spec
sections.competitorWay: Hosted or local through Docker or npm

faqs.question: Can APIForge replace Swagger Editor?
faqs.answer: No. APIForge does not edit specs, and it does not cover AsyncAPI or local-only use. It is a better fit once a spec exists and you want to score it, send requests and generate tests.

faqs.question: Do APIForge and Swagger Editor work together?
faqs.answer: Yes. Write and validate the spec in Swagger Editor, publish it, then load the published URL in APIForge to see its design score and test the API.

faqs.question: Does APIForge support both OpenAPI 3.0 and Swagger 2.0?
faqs.answer: Yes. It loads Swagger 2.0 and OpenAPI 3.x files from a URL, a Swagger UI page, or an upload. In our test its parser also loaded 3.1 and 3.2 files, and files whose version field Swagger UI rejects.
